dedupe_keys.name: do thermal comfort standards ensure occupant satisfaction learning from occupants thermal complaints

description: Kocaman, Ezgi and colleagues publish this resource through Zenodo. The principal Paris case evaluates PMV against 53 submitted thermal complaints from January 2017 to May 2018. PMV indicates four-percent dissatisfaction under the corresponding conditions, while every selected complaint expresses dissatisfaction. The latter is a complaint-selected sample, not population-wide prevalence. A related French cooling-season study compares 100 actual/predicted thermal-sensation observations by gender and age. The shared research team and programme justify one grouped assessment family, while exact participant or campaign overlap remains unknown. A 93-person survey-participation study supplies response-selection context. These applications assess model limitations and should not be read as universal demographic correction factors. Native metadata gives open access and the licence label cc-by-4.0. These terms describe the deposit; a paper licence does not establish a software licence. Coverage is limited to the stated sites, model settings and application examples. Only descriptive metadata and file descriptors were inspected. Linked data, code and document bodies were not opened.
